Claims that do not apply to this implementation, with the reason:

| ECMA clause | Claim ID | Module | Claim | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1.3 | A-4.1.3-EX | core | The examples of the character section are declared empty, so no example program of section 4.1.3 needs to be accepted or run. | Section 4.1.3 declares 'Examples: None' (l.1124-1127), so there is no example program to accept or run. |
| 4.4.6 | A-4.4.6-01 | core | An implementation may add extra built-in functions, but a declaration of such a name in a program unit must override the built-in meaning there. | This implementation supplies no built-in functions beyond those of the standard (the parser's supplied-function lists match l.1885-1888 and the string list of 6.4), so there is no extra built-in whose meaning a declaration could override. |
| 4.4.6 | A-4.4.6-02 | core | An implementation offering parameterless enhancement functions must also give a syntax to tell them apart from plain variables, such as requiring a declaration or empty parentheses at each call. | No parameterless enhancement functions are supplied (the only no-argument supplied names are the standard's own reserved ones), so no distinguishing syntax is required. |
| 7.2.6 | E-1505 | core | Reporting an array expression underflow as exception 1505 is only a recommendation. | Table 9 lists 1505 as recommended and not mandated, so the standard requires no behaviour to test (the required behaviour, replacing the value by zero, is claim A-7.2.4.2-07). |
| 11.1.5 | E-7052 | files | Opening a device as a RELATIVE or KEYED file raises the fatal exception 7052. | The portable suite has a single device, the console on channel zero; OPEN on channel zero with any organization yields nonfatal 7002 (E-7002, FIL-0077) and NAME 'CONSOLE' creates a true file, so no device can be opened as RELATIVE/KEYED. Mandated at Table 9 l.12913. On POSIX hosts this interpreter also treats a file that is not regular (for example /dev/null) as a device and raises 7052; that is tested in FullBasicCoreXCTests/ComplianceFIOla2AXCTests. |
| 11.1.5 | E-7311 | files | ERASE on an OUTIN device without erase capability raises the nonfatal exception 7311: nothing is erased and execution continues. | The only device in the portable suite is the console on channel zero; ERASE on channel zero yields nonfatal 7002 (E-7002, FIL-0077), so 7311 cannot occur. Mandated at Table 9 l.12934. On POSIX hosts ERASE on a non-regular file opened with OUTIN (for example /dev/null) raises 7311, and ASK ERASABLE gives NO; that is tested in FullBasicCoreXCTests/ComplianceFIOla2AXCTests. |
| 11.2.5 | E-7205 | files | A record-setter on a device without that capability raises the nonfatal exception 7205: the pointer does not move and execution continues. | The only device is the console on channel zero, and any record-setter on channel zero yields nonfatal 7002 (E-7002, FIL-0077); no other device exists, so 7205 cannot occur. Mandated at Table 9 l.12919. |
| 11.4 | E-1508 | files | Treating a numeric underflow during file input as the nonfatal exception 1508 (supply zero and continue) is only recommended, not mandated, so no behaviour is required. | Table 9 l.12823 marks 1508 as recommended, not mandated ('I 1508'), and 11.4 l.8462 says 'is recommended'; the interpreter supplies zero without raising 1508. |

## 8. Limits of the evidence

- **Self-declaration, not certification.** This document is published by the implementer. ECMA-116 (BASIC), mapped through the `ecma` field of each claim defines conformance but does not certify implementations, and no external body has tested or endorsed this one: the claims are backed only by the programs listed above, run on the platform and at the commit identified in section 2.
- **What a program can prove.** That this interpreter accepts, rejects or executes each specific program with the specific result recorded, on that host. It cannot prove anything about programs not run, other hosts, platforms, operating-system versions or commits.
- **Real time (ANSI §14) is not claimed** and cannot be probed by this suite: no real-time programs, parallel sections or event handling are run (ANSI §14; ECMA-116 §2.5).
- **Editing (ANSI §16) is not claimed** as a module; editing is provided by the host application's editor, not by §16 commands in the program text (section 7).
- **Devices other than the console and files.** The command-line host exposes a single device, the console on channel zero, so exceptions that require another device (for example 7205 and 7311, Table 9 l.12919 and l.12934) cannot occur and are marked not applicable in section 7.
- **The wording of default exception reports** beyond the exception code and the line number is implementation-defined (§2.4 l.617-620); the tests check the code and the line, not the text around them.
- **Graphics** are compared through the interpreter's primitive trace (`--draw-log {drawlog}`), not by inspecting a rendered screen. The trace records the primitives, the window, viewport, clip, text-justify and color-mix settings and the values ASK returns, but not the line style, point style or color a primitive is drawn with, and it records the primitives before clipping, which the host renderer does: how each style and color looks, and the clipping itself, are checked only through ASK.
- **Resource-constraint exceptions** (§2.4 l.593-595) depend on the host's memory and limits; only the tested cases are claimed. Numeric precision and range are implementation-defined (Appendix C, §5.6) and are declared in section 5.
- **Absence is not evidence.** Clauses without a listed claim (the pending counts in the header and in section 3) are not a statement of non-conformance.
